basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 21.' and it opens 'VERS. 21.-- Habitavitque in deserto Pharan. Pharan nunc oppidum [ Z., Faron oppidum,'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 21.-- Habitavitque in deserto Pharan. Pharan nunc oppidum [ Z., Faron oppidum, etc.] trans Arabiam junctum Saracenis, qui in solitudine vagi errant. Per hoc transierunt filii Israel, cum de monte Sina castra movissent. Est autem trans Arabiam, ut diximus, contra australem plagam, et distat ab Aelia contra orientem itinere dierum trium. Ibi habitasse Ismaelem dicitur, unde et Ismaelitae, qui nunc Saraceni dicuntur.
